\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
A program is a few functions that the runtime calls; each line is one instruction; values live in registers while they are computed and in memory between frames. Everything else you used today has a lecture of its own. Next: where these ideas came from.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item Read the line  loop:  li a0, 32   \# x  aloud. Name its label, instruction, operands and comment. Is li an instruction of the processor? What does the assembler do with it?
\item The debugger shows the instruction addi t1, t1, 1 stored in memory as the word 0x00130313. What is that word, and what does it tell you about where a program lives?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
